name: STR-1
def: Radio controlled clearing robot derived from Lunokhod chassis work, used on the reactor building roofs at Chernobyl in 1986.
body: VNII Transmash drew on its planetary rover experience, beginning with Lunokhod 1, to build a remotely driven machine that could work in radiation fields lethal to people. The robot was fitted with a blade to push highly radioactive debris off the roofs beside the destroyed reactor, and was driven by radio from a shielded position with help from mast mounted television cameras. Working from 8 August to 10 October 1986 the machines cleared about 90 tonnes of radioactive material and kept roughly a thousand people out of the most dangerous zone.
facts: Cleared about 90 tonnes of radioactive debris from Chernobyl roofs
Worked from 8 August to 10 October 1986 where people could not go
specs: Wheeled chassis derived from the Lunokhod self propelled chassis with a bulldozer blade
Silver zinc batteries giving several hours of work per charge
Mast mounted television cameras providing the operator's view
Radio teleoperation from a shielded control point
